entry.title: After the Fall
entry.content:
Book

The book featured in my art groups with seniors this week was “After the Fall: How Humpty Dumpty Got Back Up Again” by Dan Santat. It is a perfect read for leading an art discussion on fears, confidence, and bravery.

Response Art

The art process includes drawing or coloring in a brick wall that represents a fear or a personal problem while thinking about the walls’ height in relation to your experience of the problem. For my older adults, I found preprinted coloring pages of brick walls and cutting a 8.5x 11 standard size paper in half as the most-less intimidating approach. Then, I folded the paper into a paper plane to represent our ability to reach past fears or problems. If you want, add personal self-affirmations onto the paper plane.

Therapeutic Benefits

The artwork evokes conversation around perseverance through trials, resulting in a collective understanding of human struggle and resiliency. The overall process promotes a sense of agency, building self-esteem, problem solving, and positive thinking.

Materials

Coloring paper, coloring pencils/pens, pencil and eraser
entry.summary: A perfect read for leading an art discussion on fears, confidence, and bravery

entry.title: MLK Day Reflections
entry.content:
Book

This week, I used the book “Martin Rising” by Andrea Davis Pinkney & Brian Pinkney with seniors. We reflected on community, connection, and unity through art.

Response Art

The process includes reading a select few poems from the book, discussing the themes, and tracing our hands or coloring paper in the shape of a hand to personalize with words or images. Participants were asked to add imagery or words that help them explore the content deeper, and to apply the content to their own lives if desired.

Therapeutic Benefits

The artwork evokes conversation around our own personal values and need for action. The overall process promotes a sense of agency and independence, increasing interpersonal skills and self-awareness.

Materials

Skintone craft paper, coloring pencils/pens, gem stickers, gluestick, scissors, pencil
entry.summary: This week, I used the book "Martin Rising" by Andrea Davis Pinkney & Brian Pinkney with seniors. We reflected on community, connection, and unity through art.
